reading: Each straight red segment becomes the diagonal of a filled diamond of colour 8: a background cell at perpendicular distance D>=1 from the segment is filled if it lies at least D cells inside both segment ends.

new_rows.name: dia
new_rows.datalog:
lo(O, min(X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
hi(O, max(X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
top(O, min(Y)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
bot(O, max(Y)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
horiz(O, Y, L, H) :- obj(O, Y, X), top(O, Y), bot(O, Y), lo(O, L), hi(O, H).
vert(O, X, T, U) :- obj(O, Y, X), lo(O, X), hi(O, X), top(O, T), bot(O, U).
dia(Y2, X) :- horiz(O, Y, L, H), px(Y2, X, C), !fgc(Y2, X), D = Y2 - Y, D >= 1, A = X - L, A >= D, B = H - X, B >= D.
dia(Y2, X) :- horiz(O, Y, L, H), px(Y2, X, C), !fgc(Y2, X), D = Y - Y2, D >= 1, A = X - L, A >= D, B = H - X, B >= D.
dia(Y, X2) :- vert(O, X, T, U), px(Y, X2, C), !fgc(Y, X2), D = X2 - X, D >= 1, A = Y - T, A >= D, B = U - Y, B >= D.
dia(Y, X2) :- vert(O, X, T, U), px(Y, X2, C), !fgc(Y, X2), D = X - X2, D >= 1, A = Y - T, A >= D, B = U - Y, B >= D.

why: every 8 cell is inside the diamond whose diagonal is a red segment; red cells and other background unchanged

reading: The 9 coloured cells of the 5x5 X pattern are gathered into a 3x3: corners stay corners, centre stays centre, and the four inner diagonal cells move to the edge midpoints (top-left inner to top, top-right inner to right, bottom-left inner to left, bottom-right inner to bottom).

slots.source: the 9 non-background cells of the X (corners, inner diagonal, centre)
slots.layout: corners->3x3 corners, centre->centre, inner diagonals->edge midpoints (rotated 45 degrees)

why: output cells are exactly the input's non-background cells, repositioned; no background left

reading: The grid is a 3x3 array of 2x2 panels. When two cells of the same special colour (not 0, not 1) sit in the same row or column at the same position of two panels, the corresponding cell of the panel midway between them takes that colour.

new_rows.name: mid
new_rows.datalog:
mk(Y, X, C) :- cell(Y, X, C), C > 1.
mid(Y, X) :- mk(Y, X1, C), mk(Y, X2, C), px(Y, X, B), D = X - X1, D > 0, X2 = X + D.
mid(Y, X) :- mk(Y1, X, C), mk(Y2, X, C), px(Y, X, B), D = Y - Y1, D > 0, Y2 = Y + D.

slots.colour: the colour of the two equal marks the midpoint lies between

why: each changed cell is the exact midpoint of two same-coloured marks on one row or column and takes their colour

reading: An n x n input is tiled n times across and n times down (every block is a copy of the input).
why: output is (n*h) x (n*w) with n = input side; every block equals the input

reading: A large object cut off by the grid edge is a 2x-scaled, cropped copy of one of the small objects; the output is the bounding box of that matching small object.
verb: select shape matching the big one

slots.reference: the large object touching the grid edge (2x-scaled, cropped)
slots.test: candidate whose 2x upscale contains the visible part of the reference
slots.output: the matching candidate's box cut from the input (with background)

why: exactly one small object, scaled by 2, agrees with the visible part of the big edge object

reading: Three 4x4 panels separated by colour-2 columns are overlaid into one 4x4; at each cell the first panel's colour wins (4), else the second's (9), else the third's (1), else 0.

slots.parts: panels cut by the separator columns of colour 2
slots.order: left panel over middle over right (4 > 9 > 1 > 0)

why: each output cell is the non-background colour of the leftmost panel that has one there

reading: The 8x8 interior is four 4x4 quadrants: the top-left pattern is copied mirrored into the other three (left-right, top-bottom, rotated 180), and each copy's colours are remapped using the hint cells already in that quadrant; colours with no hint become 0.

slots.copies: horizontal mirror to top-right, vertical mirror to bottom-left, 180 rotation to bottom-right
slots.key: per quadrant: each hint cell maps the exemplar colour at its mirrored position to the hint colour; unhinted colours -> 0

why: each quadrant is the mirrored exemplar under a colour map consistent with every hint in it

reading: Empty columns are deleted and the shapes are chained left to right: each shape is shifted vertically so its leftmost cell sits on the row where the previous shape's path ends at its right side.

slots.subject: the shapes, separated by empty columns
slots.shift: vertical offset so each shape's left-end cell meets the previous shape's right-end row, forming one continuous path

why: output width = input width minus empty columns; shapes keep shape and colour and form one connected chain

reading: Every coloured cell draws a line of its own colour straight down to the bottom border.
why: each column below a coloured cell is filled with that colour down to the border

reading: From the single 8 cell a fixed staircase of 5s is drawn up-right and (mirrored) down-left: one step out, then three cells sideways, repeating, clipped at the grid edge.
why: the 5 cells are the same offset pattern relative to the 8 in every pair (clipped at the border)
